title: An illustrated step-by-step guide to establish a disinfection facility for reuse of personal protective equipment
protocol: Segregate used PPE by the users at the doffing site as per institutional guidelines.
Discard used PPE that are weakened in strength, torn, soaking-wet, or heavily soiled with patients’ body fluids.
Place intact or minimally stained used PPE in a designated “Used PPE” biohazard bin for potential reuse after disinfection.
Bag used PPE after collection.
Wipe bag with 0.5% hypochlorite on the outside.
Double-bag the first bag and wipe the second bag's exterior with 0.5% hypochlorite.
Hand over double-bagged PPE to another HCW for further transportation.
Collect used PPE bags in a designated trolley if the disinfection facility is nearby.
Transport trolley with used PPE to the PPE Disinfection Facility.
Transport used PPE from storage area to the disinfection area.
Ensure the disinfection area is equipped with electrical supply and UPS/generator backup.
Provide access to distilled/autoclaved water, measuring cylinders, and hand hygiene accessories in the disinfection area.
Make sure the room is air-tight to ensure proper exposure time for VHP disinfection.
Verify that the room size is compatible with the capacity of the VHP machine.
Transport used PPE bags to the gate of the VHP disinfection room using a dedicated wheel cart/trolley.
Carry the required number of bags inside the room and keep them close to the door.
Manually program the VHP machine as per the room dimensions and add the required volume of hydrogen peroxide solution.
Open Used PPE bags individually to take out the inner bag.
Carry the inner bag towards the end of the room.
Adhere to manufacturer’s instructions to operate the VHP machine.
Press the start button after proper setup.
Exit the room through the door towards the dirty area.
Seal the room door from the outside upon exit.
Recommend a minimum of 1 to 1.5 hours contact time post-run for disinfection and vapour clearance.
Do not open the room early to avoid H2O2 residual vapor irritation.
Clean the machine at the end of the day as per the manufacturer’s instructions.
Use a 10 min cycle with distilled water for nozzle cleaning and prevent clogging.
Collect exposed biological indicators in respective media tubes after entry into the room via the “clean area”.
Seal, pack, and wipe clean the tubes containing spore strips in brain heart infusion broth or tryptic soy broth.
Pass the sealed and cleaned tubes over to a HCW standing in the “clean area” outside the room.
Transfer control strips outside the room.
Collect disinfected PPE and pack it in bags.
Label bags with the disinfection cycle number and date.
Wipe bags with 0.5% sodium hypochlorite before handing over to the second HCW standing in the clean area.
Keep disinfected bags in a dedicated area until test results confirm successful disinfection.
Do not open disinfected bags until quality assurance confirms success.
If disinfection fails, return the bags to the disinfection room and process them like other used PPE.
After handing over disinfected PPE, the worker may continue working or prepare for the next cycle.
The worker can also move to the doffing area, change, and exit the facility.
Transport indicator tubes to the culture facility after disinfection.
Incubate indicator tubes at 55°C for 3-5 days under shaking conditions (180 rpm) as per manufacturer’s instructions.
Transfer bags to the post-disinfection processing area once successful disinfection is established.
Open the bags and check for small spots or stains using cleaning agents like 70% ethanol or 0.1% hypochlorite as quality checks.
Discard any torn PPE or N-95 masks found during inspection.
Complete the post-disinfection quality check before packaging.
Package and distribute the decontaminated PPE as needed.
Disinfect and check PPE for physical integrity.
Ensure no deformities exist in the PPE after disinfection cycles.
Use appropriate biological indicators in the room for each cycle.
If the room is larger than 2000 cubic feet, use two biological indicators at both ends of the room.
Catalogue disinfected PPE to track the number of disinfection cycles.
